_: EP 17 — VectorDrop's storage migration, Supabase → Cloudflare R2. The STATION STRIP register (references/station-strip.md), built on VectorDrop's OWN dark-mode design system rather than the house look: #161516 ground, #0D0D0D panels, teal #14B8A6 as the single accent, #0D9488 demoted to hover and living only in the gradient, cyan #0891B2 only ever inside a gradient, pure #FFFFFF text. Type is the system UI face the brand's own fallback stack names — SF Pro, loaded from /System/Library/Fonts/SFNS.ttf — with Geist Mono for every path, figure and code line. EVERY NUMBER ON SCREEN IS FROM THE MIGRATION WRITE-UP: 1,156 distinct objects / 1.74 GB / ~1.53 MB average / 8.2 MB largest SVG against a 1 GB free tier; R2's free allowance is 10 GB storage, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations; S3 egress is ~$0.09/GB and R2's is zero; the crash was NGHTTP2_INTERNAL_ERROR at object 25 of 1,156 with a bare Promise.all and a pipeline that still exited 0; the HEAD size discrepancy was 1,743 MB vs 468 MB, resolved to 1,743.04 MB with Accept-Encoding: identity; the SDK signed x-amz-checksum-crc32=AAAAAA== (CRC32 of empty) because presigning happens before a body exists, fixed with requestChecksumCalculation: WHEN_REQUIRED; final result 1,091 copied + 45 already present = 1,136 of 1,136, 1.69 GB, 0 failed, 0 database rows rewritten, 20 pre-existing broken rows.
title: The Meter Ran Out.
subtitle: Moving 1.69 GB to R2 without rewriting a single database row
hook: The free tier ended. Uploads stopped. Nothing else was broken.
next: Next: presigned URLs, and the five ways they lie to you
_theme: New palette this episode — `vectordrop`, straight out of the product's DESIGN.md dark mode. The series continuity is the CONSTRUCTION and the cue set, never the colour; EP15/16 shared stripe-mesh for two episodes and this is the deliberate turn. Teal is the only filled hue on the frame: the gradient (#0D9488 → #14B8A6 → #0891B2 at 135°) is reserved for the title word and nothing else, exactly as the brand reserves it for the hero.
_voice: Unchanged from EP 13–16 — same voice id, same model, same settings. The palette turns; the narrator does not.
_music: Same 84bpm grid as EP 13–16 so scene lengths snap identically across the run.
_vo: Ten lines. Directive throughout — every line opens on an instruction verb. Definition then consequence, one clause a sentence. The five failures are stated as things the viewer should DO about them, not as things that happened to us.

vo.text:
Watch a free tier run out. One gigabyte of storage, one point seven used…
and uploads stopped working.
Understand the shape first. A two hundred kilobyte photo traces into a multi-megabyte vector.
Now choose on egress, not storage. R2 charges nothing to send your data back out.
Move the broken thing, not its neighbours. Storage was full. Postgres was fine, so Postgres stayed.
Keep the object keys byte for byte. Every path already in the database still resolves.
Watch this one closely. Presigning is local maths — it signs URLs for files that never existed.
Distrust a confident plan. Bad credentials and an empty bucket produce identical output.
Chase the discrepancy. Supabase reported gzipped bytes, R2 reports raw, so nothing ever matched.
Budget for the transient failure. One dropped connection took down all eight workers at object twenty-five.
Then check the browser. Your storage host is now part of the frontend's security policy.

_shots: No Kling. The station-strip register carries a full episode on graphics alone — the surface is the product's own dark UI, and the depth comes from real panels rather than footage.
